newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: GPA Q1 post-exceptional net profit $15 mln.
newsitem.headline: GPA Q1 post-exceptional net profit $15 mln.

text.p: Irish aircraft leasing firm GPA Group Plc said on Tuesday that it made a net profit of $15 million in the quarter ended June 30 after exceptional gains of $18 million.
The exceptional gains arose mainly from the sale of securities held in a U.S. airline, GPA said in a statement.
The group reported a net loss of $8 million after exceptional costs of $5 million in the first quarter in 1995.

Commenting on the results, chief executive Patrick Blaney said: "The market outlook for leased jet aircraft remains positive although the turboprop sector has been slow to respond to the general improvement in market conditions."
GPA said first quarter revenue fell to $94 million from $244 million in the same period last year.
Net interest expense fell to $7 million from $86 million while cashflow was down to $5 million from $153 million.

GPA said the fall in revenue, net interest expense and cashflow and the reduction in total assets to $1.97 billion from $5.95 billion arose from the sale of 229 aircraft to Airplanes Group in March 1996 as part of the refinancing of GPA's debt obligations.
Shareholders' funds at June 30 amounted to $181 million while borrowing fell to $1.19 billion from $4.55 billion.
The fall in borrowings followed prepayments of $385 million of unsecured debt under a debt buyback programme during the first quarter, GPA said.
Since the end of June, prepayments have been increased to $500 million.
